title: 'The Fall of the House of Usher,' by Edgar Allan Poe, Part Three
titleZh: 爱伦·坡的《厄舍屋的倒塌》第三部分

sentences.en: I was visiting an old friend of mine, Roderick Usher, in his old stone house, his palace, where a feeling of death hung on the air.
sentences.zh: 我去拜访老朋友罗德里克·厄舍，他住在他那座古老的石屋里，那座宫殿里，空气中弥漫着死亡的气息。

sentences.en: I saw how fear was pressing on his heart and mind.
sentences.zh: 我看见恐惧正压迫着他的心和理智。

sentences.en: Now his only sister, the lady Madeline, had died and we had put her body in its resting place, in a room inside the cold walls of the palace, a damp, dark vault, a fearful place.
sentences.zh: 如今他唯一的妹妹，玛德琳小姐已经死去，我们把她的遗体安放在安息之处，放在宫殿冰冷墙壁内的一间房间里，那是一处潮湿幽暗的地窖，一个令人恐惧的地方。

sentences.en: As we looked down upon her face, I saw that there was a strong likeness between the two.
sentences.zh: 当我们俯身凝视她的面容时，我发现两人有着极强的相似之处。

sentences.en: “Indeed,” said Usher, “we were born on the same day, and the tie between us has always been strong.”
sentences.zh: “确实，”厄舍说，“我们出生在同一天，我们之间的纽带一直都很牢固。”

sentences.en: We did not long look down at her, for fear and wonder filled our hearts.
sentences.zh: 我们没有久久俯视她的面容，因为恐惧和惊奇充满了我们的心。

sentences.en: There was still a little color in her face and there seemed to be a smile on her lips.
sentences.zh: 她的脸上仍带着一丝血色，嘴角似乎还挂着一抹微笑。

sentences.en: We closed the heavy iron door and returned to the rooms above, which were hardly less gloomy than the vault.
sentences.zh: 我们合上沉重的铁门，回到楼上的房间，那些房间几乎和地窖一样阴森。

sentences.en: And now a change came in the sickness of my friend’s mind.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我朋友的精神状态发生了变化。

sentences.en: He went from room to room with a hurried step.
sentences.zh: 他迈着匆忙的步伐，一间屋接着一间屋地走动。

sentences.en: His face was, if possible, whiter and more ghastly than before, and the light in his eyes had gone.
sentences.zh: 他的脸，如果可能的话，比先前更苍白、更吓人，眼中也失去了光彩。

sentences.en: The trembling in his voice seemed to show the greatest fear.
sentences.zh: 他声音中的颤抖似乎显示出极大的恐惧。

sentences.en: At times he sat looking at nothing for hours, as if listening to some sound I could not hear.
sentences.zh: 有时他坐着，对着空气凝视数小时，仿佛在聆听某种我听不见的声音。

sentences.en: I felt his condition, slowly but certainly, gaining power over me; I felt that his wild ideas were becoming fixed in my own mind.
sentences.zh: 我感受到他的状况正缓慢却坚定地上控于我；我感到他那些疯狂的念头正逐渐在我自己的头脑中固化。

sentences.en: As I was going to bed late in the night of the seventh or eighth day after we placed the lady Madeline within the vault, I experienced the full power of such feelings.
sentences.zh: 当我们把玛德琳小姐安葬于地窖后的第七或第八天深夜，我正要上床睡觉时，我充分体验到了这类情感的全部力量。

sentences.en: Sleep did not come — while the hours passed.
sentences.zh: 时间流逝，却迟迟无法入睡。

sentences.en: My mind fought against the nervousness.
sentences.zh: 我的头脑与这种紧张不安作着斗争。

sentences.en: I tried to believe that much, if not all, of what I felt was due to the gloomy room, to the dark wall coverings, which in a rising wind moved on the walls.
sentences.zh: 我试图相信，我所感受到的许多，即便不是全部，也都归因于这间阴森的房间，归因于那些深色的墙面装饰，它们在渐起的风中于墙上摇曳。

sentences.en: But my efforts were useless.
sentences.zh: 但我的努力都是徒劳的。

sentences.en: A trembling I could not stop filled my body, and fear without reason caught my heart.
sentences.zh: 一种我无法制止的颤抖充满了我的身体，无缘无故的恐惧攫住了我的心。

sentences.en: I sat up, looking into the darkness of my room, listening — I do not know why — to certain low sounds which came when the storm was quiet.
sentences.zh: 我坐起身，凝视着房间的黑暗，倾听着——我也不知道为什么——那些在风暴平息时传来的低沉声响。

sentences.en: A feeling of horror lay upon me like a heavy weight.
sentences.zh: 一种恐怖的感觉像沉重的负担一样压在我身上。

sentences.en: I put on my clothes and began walking nervously around the room.
sentences.zh: 我穿上衣服，开始在房间里 nervously 地走来走去。

sentences.en: I had been walking for a very short time when I heard a light step coming toward my door.
sentences.zh: 我走了很短的时间，就听到一阵轻快的脚步声朝我的门走来。

sentences.en: I knew it was Usher.
sentences.zh: 我知道那是厄舍尔。

sentences.en: In a moment I saw him at my door, as usual very white, but there was a wild laugh in his eyes.
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，我就看到他在我的门口，像往常一样苍白，但他的眼睛里却带着一种狂野的笑声。

sentences.en: Even so, I was glad to have his company.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，我还是很高兴有他的陪伴。

sentences.en: “And have you not seen it?” he said.
sentences.zh: “难道你没有见过它吗？”他说。

sentences.en: He hurried to one of the windows and opened it to the storm.
sentences.zh: 他急忙走到一扇窗前，把它打开，迎向风暴。

sentences.en: The force of the entering wind nearly lifted us from our feet.
sentences.zh: 涌入的风的力量几乎把我们从脚上掀起来。

sentences.en: It was, indeed, a stormy but beautiful night, and wildly strange.
sentences.zh: 确实，那是一个风雨交加却美丽的夜晚，狂野而奇异。

sentences.en: The heavy, low-hanging clouds which seemed to press down upon the house, flew from all directions against each other, always returning and never passing away in the distance.
sentences.zh: 那些沉重的、低垂的、似乎压在房子上的云，从各个方向相互碰撞，总是回来，却永远不消散在远方。

sentences.en: With their great thickness they cut off all light from the moon and the stars.
sentences.zh: 凭借它们巨大的厚度，它们挡住了月亮和星星的所有光芒。

sentences.en: But we could see them because they were lighted from below by the air itself, which we could see, rising from the dark lake and from the stones of the house itself.
sentences.zh: 但我们能看到它们，因为它们从下方被空气照亮，而空气本身我们也能看到，从黑暗的湖水和房子本身的石头上升起。

sentences.en: “You must not — you shall not look out at this!”
sentences.zh: “你不该——你不许往外面看这个！”

sentences.en: I said to Usher, as I led him from the window to a seat.
sentences.zh: 我对厄舍尔说，当我把他从窗边引到座位上时。

sentences.en: “This appearance which surprises you so has been seen in other places, too.
sentences.zh: “这种景象你如此惊讶，其实在别处也见过。

sentences.en: Perhaps the lake is the cause.
sentences.zh: 也许是湖水造成的。

sentences.en: Let us close this window; the air is cold.
sentences.zh: 让我们把这扇窗关上；空气很冷。

sentences.en: Here is one of the stories you like best.
sentences.zh: 这里有一部你最喜欢的故事。

sentences.en: I will read and you shall listen and thus we will live through this fearful night together.”
sentences.zh: “我会读给你听，你也来听，这样我们就能一起熬过这可怕的夜晚。”

sentences.en: The old book which I had picked up was one written by a fool for fools to read, and it was not, in truth, one that Usher liked.
sentences.zh: 我随手拿起的那本书，是一位愚人写给愚人看的，事实上，拉舍尔也并不喜欢它。

sentences.en: It was, however, the only one within easy reach.
sentences.zh: 然而，它是离手边最近的一本书。

sentences.en: He seemed to listen quietly.
sentences.zh: 他似乎静静地听着。

sentences.en: Then I came to a part of the story in which a man, a strong man full of wine, begins to break down a door, and the sound of the dry wood as it breaks can be heard through all the forest around him.
sentences.zh: 接着，我读到了故事中这样一个部分：一个男人，一个酒足饭饱的壮汉，开始砸门，那干燥的木头被砸裂的声音，能传遍他四周整片森林。

sentences.en: Here I stopped, for it seemed to me that from some very distant part of the house sounds came to my ears like those of which I had been reading.
sentences.zh: 就在这里我停下了，因为我觉得，从房子某个极其遥远的地方，传来了一些声音，与我正在读的那些声音十分相似。

sentences.en: It must have been this likeness that had made me notice them, for the sounds themselves, with the storm still increasing, were nothing to stop or interest me.
sentences.zh: 想必正是这种相似，才让我注意到了它们，因为那些声音本身，伴随着风暴仍在加剧，根本不足以让我停下或产生兴趣。

sentences.en: I continued the story, and read how the man, now entering through the broken door, discovers a strange and terrible animal of the kind so often found in these old stories.
sentences.zh: 我继续读下去，读到那个男人如今从砸裂的门中闯入，发现了一种如此类故事中常见的奇异而可怕的动物。

sentences.en: He strikes it and it falls, with such a cry that he has to close his ears with his hands.
sentences.zh: 他一击打它，它就倒下，发出一声尖叫，让他不得不用手捂住耳朵。

sentences.en: Here again I stopped.
sentences.zh: 这一次，我又停下了。

sentences.en: There could be no doubt.
sentences.zh: 这绝不会有错。

sentences.en: This time I did hear a distant sound, very much like the cry of the animal in the story.
sentences.zh: 这一次，我确实听到了一种遥远的声音，与故事中那只动物的叫声极为相似。

sentences.en: I tried to control myself so that my friend would see nothing of what I felt.
sentences.zh: 我努力控制自己，好让我的朋友看不出我内心的任何一丝感受。

sentences.en: I was not certain that he had heard the sound, although he had clearly changed in some way.
sentences.zh: 他是否也听到了那声音，我并不能确定，尽管他显然在某方面有了变化。

sentences.en: He had slowly moved his chair so that I could not see him well.
sentences.zh: 他缓缓挪动了自己的椅子，让我无法看清他。

sentences.en: I did see that his lips were moving as if he were speaking to himself.
sentences.zh: 我却看到他的嘴唇在动，仿佛他正在自言自语。

sentences.en: His head had dropped forward, but I knew he was not asleep, for his eyes were open and he was moving his body from side to side.
sentences.zh: 他的头低垂下来，但我知道他并未睡着，因为他的眼睛睁着，身体还在左右摇晃。

sentences.en: I began reading again, and quickly came to a part of the story where a heavy piece of iron falls on a stone floor with a ringing sound.
sentences.zh: 我重新开始读，很快读到了故事中这样一个部分：一块沉重的铁器砸在石地板上，发出清脆的响声。

sentences.en: These words had just passed my lips when I heard clearly, but from far away, a loud ringing sound — as if something of iron had indeed fallen heavily upon a stone floor, or as if an iron door had closed.
sentences.zh: 这些话刚从我唇边掠过，我就清晰地听到——虽来自远处——一声响亮的金属轰鸣声，仿佛真有铁器重重地砸在石地板上，又仿佛一扇铁门关上了。

sentences.en: I lost control of myself completely, and jumped up from my chair.
sentences.zh: 我完全失去了对自己的控制，猛地从椅子上跳了起来。

sentences.en: Usher still sat, moving a little from side to side.
sentences.zh: 厄舍仍坐着，身子微微左右晃动。

sentences.en: His eyes were turned to the floor.
sentences.zh: 他的目光投向地板。

sentences.en: I rushed to his chair.
sentences.zh: 我奔向他的座椅。

sentences.en: As I placed my hand on his shoulder, I felt that his whole body was trembling; a sickly smile touched his lips; he spoke in a low, quick, and nervous voice as if he did not know I was there.
sentences.zh: 当我把手放在他肩上时，感到他全身都在颤抖；一抹病态的微笑掠过他的唇边；他用低沉、急促而神经质的声音说话，仿佛并不知道我就在一旁。

sentences.en: “Yes!” he said.
sentences.zh: “是的！”他说。

sentences.en: “I heard it!
sentences.zh: “我听见了！

sentences.en: Many minutes, many hours, many days have I heard it — but I did not dare to speak!
sentences.zh: 许多分钟，许多小时，许多天，我都在听着——可我不敢开口！

sentences.en: We have put her living in the vault!
sentences.zh: 我们把她活埋在地窖里了！

sentences.en: Did I not say that my senses were too strong?
sentences.zh: 我是不是说过，我的感官过于敏锐？

sentences.en: I heard her first movements many days ago — yet I did not dare to speak!
sentences.zh: 许多天前我就听见她最初的动静——可我不敢开口！

sentences.en: And now, that story — but the sounds were hers!
sentences.zh: 而现在，那个故事——但那声音分明是她发出的！

sentences.en: Oh, where shall I run?!
sentences.zh: 哦，我该往哪儿逃？！

sentences.en: She is coming — coming to ask why I put her there too soon.
sentences.zh: 她来了——来问我为何这么早就把她埋了进去。

sentences.en: I hear her footsteps on the stairs.
sentences.zh: 我听见她脚步踏上了楼梯。

sentences.en: I hear the heavy beating of her heart.”
sentences.zh: 我听见她心脏沉重的跳动。”

sentences.en: Here he jumped up and cried as if he were giving up his soul: “I tell you, she now stands at the door!!”
sentences.zh: 说到这里，他猛地跳起来，哭喊着，仿佛正交出他的灵魂：“我告诉你，她此刻就站在门口！！”

sentences.en: The great door to which he was pointing now slowly opened.
sentences.zh: 他所指的那扇大门此刻缓缓打开了。

sentences.en: It was the work of the rushing wind, perhaps — but no — outside that door a shape did stand, the tall figure, in its grave-clothes, of the lady Madeline of Usher.
sentences.zh: 那或许是疾风所致，也许——但不——门外确实立着一个身影，那是厄舍家族的马德琳小姐的高大身形，身着殓服。

sentences.en: There was blood upon her white dress, and the signs of her terrible efforts to escape were upon every part of her thin form.
sentences.zh: 她洁白的裙上沾着血，她那可怕的挣扎逃脱的痕迹遍布她瘦弱身躯的每一处。

sentences.en: For a moment she remained trembling at the door; then, with a low cry, she fell heavily in upon her brother; in her pain, as she died at last, she carried him down with her, down to the floor.
sentences.zh: 有那么一刻，她颤抖着立于门口；接着，一声低呼，她重重地扑倒在哥哥身上；在痛苦中，当她终于死去时，她把他一同拖倒，一直倒在地上。

sentences.en: He too was dead, killed by his own fear.
sentences.zh: 他也死了，死于他自己的恐惧。

sentences.en: I rushed from the room; I rushed from the house. I ran.
sentences.zh: 我冲出了房间；我冲出了房子。我跑了起来。

sentences.en: The storm was around me in all its strength as I crossed the bridge.
sentences.zh: 当我走过桥时，暴风雨在我四周以全部力量肆虐。

sentences.en: Suddenly a wild light moved along the ground at my feet, and I turned to see where it could have come from, for only the great house and its darkness were behind me.
sentences.zh: 突然，一道狂野的光在我脚下的地面上移动，我转身去看它可能来自何处，因为除了那座大房子及其黑暗外，我身后别无他物。

sentences.en: The light was that of the full moon, of a bloodred moon, which was now shining through that break in the front wall, that crack which I thought I had seen when I first saw the palace.
sentences.zh: 那道光是满月之光，是一轮血红的月亮，此刻正透过前墙上的那道裂缝照耀，那道裂缝正是我初次见到这座宫殿时以为看到过的。

sentences.en: Then only a little crack, it now widened as I watched.
sentences.zh: 起初只是一道小小的裂缝，如今在我注视下逐渐扩大。

sentences.en: A strong wind came rushing over me — the whole face of the moon appeared.
sentences.zh: 一阵强风扑面而来——整个月亮的面容都显现了出来。

sentences.en: I saw the great walls falling apart.
sentences.zh: 我看见那高大的墙壁正在崩塌。

sentences.en: There was a long and stormy shouting sound — and the deep black lake closed darkly over all that remained of the House of Usher.
sentences.zh: 传来一阵漫长而狂暴的呼喊声——深邃漆黑的湖水悄然合拢，覆盖了厄舍屋仅存的一切。

glossary.def: the official home of a king, queen, president, or other official
a locked room where money or valuable things are kept
the quality or state of being alike or similar especially in appearance

glossary.zh: 可怕的；令人震惊的；骇人的

glossary.def: shaking slightly because you are afraid, nervous, or excited
used to refer to a quality that is noticed but that is difficult to explain or describe
a very strong feeling of fear, dread, and shock
a feeling of being unsure about something
to move or do something very quickly or in a way that shows you are in a hurry
a person or animal that can be seen only as a shape or outline
a hole in the ground for burying a dead body
